title: A 3 mm post across WR-90, wall to wall, by the time-domain solver for solids on 0.5 mm cells, at 10 GHz
source: The full-height post is a two-dimensional problem: the parallel-plate Green's function in modes with its static part summed in closed form (Marcuvitz, Waveguide Handbook, 1951, §5.11; Lewin, Theory of Waveguides, 1975, ch. 6), the first-kind integral equation on the post solved by Kress's log-split Nyström method (Kress, Linear Integral Equations, 3rd ed., 2014, ch. 12–13), evaluated at 128 nodes (emcraft-theory::post, independent of the time domain); the reference adaptive-post checks the FEM against

quantities.reason: the post staircased on 0.5 mm cells, three cells to its radius: the cells whose centres lie outside the circle and the edges whose midpoints lie inside it make it a little thicker (|S11| 0.9665, as a post about 0.15 mm wider would give: S moves by 478 per metre of radius)
as |S11|: the staircase's thicker post, 5.3° off
as |S11|; |S21| = √(1 − |S11|²) moves three times as fast (0.2565)
